critical thinking = the skill of analysing arguments and evidence rather than accepting them
plagiarism = using someone else's words or ideas as if they were your own
gap year = a year out of formal study, often used to travel or work
drop out = to leave a course before finishing it
skip classes = to miss lessons without permission
brush up on = to improve knowledge of something you used to know better
fall behind = to progress more slowly than the course or your peers
catch up = to reach the required level after being behind
knuckle down = to start working seriously and with discipline
skim-read = to read quickly for the main points rather than every word
mind map = a diagram of ideas branching from a central topic
autonomous learner = a student who can plan, monitor and evaluate their own study
constructive feedback = comments that explain how work can be improved, not only what is wrong
time management = planning study and rest so deadlines are met without last-minute panic
procrastinate = to delay work that should be done now
study group = a small set of students who revise or solve problems together
past paper = an exam paper from a previous session, used for practice
academic integrity = honesty in study, including proper citation and no cheating
cite sources = to name the works you have used in academic writing
paraphrase = to rewrite an idea in your own words while keeping the meaning
